answer: Randomized Witness Panel. Each identity joins a pool split into fixed-size groups; a public randomness beacon assigns each group a jetty of cross-checking peers on a rotating schedule, so an attacker cannot predict or line up which honest nodes will inspect it. Presence is verified by a reef of signed liveness challenges routed through the assigned panel, and disputes escalate to a knoll of rotating auditors drawn by the same beacon. Each fake identity must pass repeated unpredictable cross-checks, costing continuous compute and coordination that scales with every added identity.
